name: stri_startswith_fixed
title: Determine if the Start or End of a String Matches a Pattern

origin.description: Report whether a literal pattern matches at a code-point position.
origin.usage: stri_startswith_fixed(str, pattern, from = 1L, negate = FALSE, ..., opts_fixed = NULL)

arguments.name: from
arguments.text: 1-based code-point index where the match must start. Negative values count from the end.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, report positions that do not match.

origin.details: str, pattern, and from are recycled together. Index 1 is the first code point and -1 is the last. An empty pattern or a missing value is NA. An empty string follows negate. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
origin.example:
found <- stri_startswith_fixed(c("a1", "a2", "b3", "a4", "c5"), "a")
cat(paste0('stri_startswith_fixed(c("a1", "a2", "b3", "a4", "c5"), "a") returns ', paste(found, collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Report whether a literal pattern matches at a code-point position.
translation.usage: stri_startswith_fixed(str, pattern, from_=1, negate=False, opts_fixed=None, case_insensitive=None, overlap=None)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Literal pattern, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.text: R's from. A 1-based code-point index. Negative values count from the end. from is reserved in Python.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, report positions that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_fixed
arguments.text: None, or a dict of search settings. Overlap is ignored.

arguments.name: case_insensitive
arguments.text: If given, compare the simple uppercase of each code point.

arguments.name: overlap
arguments.text: Ignored, as in the installed function.

translation.details: str, pattern, and from_ are recycled together. Index 1 is the first code point and -1 is the last. An empty pattern or a missing value is NA. An empty string follows negate. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
translation.value: A list of True, False, and NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.fixed import stri_startswith_fixed
found = stri_startswith_fixed(["a1", "a2", "b3", "a4", "c5"], "a")
print('stri_startswith_fixed(["a1", "a2", "b3", "a4", "c5"], "a") returns ' + ", ".join(str(item) for item in found) + ".")
